_note: PLAYER'S PART (2026-11-04, his: 'MB104a should have you rescue her'): open the container and take her aboard as a guest, then fly her to a city. Built as the rescue 2026-11-04 (Eliza), the beats from letter office/correspondence/2026-11-04-jessica-eliza-mb104a-is-a-rescue.md; proven on duo_delvetest_r2. CARD in the owners' hand, no payer label or payment line (his 11-04). HER NAME: Rosie Marlow (the person's label aboard, never spoken; Eliza's catch 11-04).
Eliza, 2026-11-04: the lines below about a recovery beacon, one beat and the closing say are the 11-03 build's, retired by the rescue; kept as history.
SPACE CARGO 5: THE WRONG MANIFEST. A container adrift in orbit, listed as machine parts. Pick it up.
THE HOOK: someone is in it, and she is the radio. The broadcast is her, calling from inside the box when the player
comes within range, so the speaker is the stowaway and the card is the owners' (unvoiced). One beat; the closing

line is the use's say. FITTED TO boardspace: a one-beat board is a use. NO TOW EXISTS (his play, 2026-11-03: activate it, then fly away), so the use fixes a recovery beacon to the hull and she stays inside for the owners' tug.

Every space Delve before these was a satellite (5 of 7); these are about CARGO, his ask. Markers: General01/06/02 and TravelB02 are 51a's and 30a's; which a cell offers is Eliza's. No names, places, factions or currency in a voiced line. Pay: med, capped, placeholder.

prose.name: Recovery: Lost Container over <Planet>
prose.briefing: A cargo container slipped its mooring during a transfer over <Planet> and has been drifting ever since. The owners want it picked up. The manifest says machine parts.
prose.card: Container lost over <Planet> during a transfer, four days adrift. Manifest says machine parts. Find it and bring it in.

beats.name: Drifting Cargo Container

message.title: Drifting Cargo Container
message.text: The lock is on the outside. You open it, and she climbs straight across into your airlock.

greeting: I've never been so glad to see the inside of someone else's ship. I'll stay out of your way. Where do you want me?

exchanges.prompt: Sit anywhere. I'll get you to a city.
How did you end up in a cargo box?
reply: I needed a way off that rock, and the box was going. It seemed like a good idea for about an hour.
Hungry. Stiff. Very tired of the dark. Nothing a city won't fix.

beats.journal: The container over <Planet> wasn't machine parts. A woman had spent four days in it. I took her aboard and flew her to <SecondPlace>.
greeting: PLACEHOLDER, Jessica's: she thanks him at the ramp.

broadcast: Is that a ship? Please be a ship. I've been in this box four days and the air scrubber's started making a noise I don't like, so if you're here for the container, I'm in it.
_speech: Young, frightened, trying to be funny about it. Lucy (Fresh and Casual), from remote06b; his ear decides.
